reasoning_traces.think:
The SHARP framework addresses core challenges in autonomous financial agents: unbounded free-form adaptation leads to policy drift due to poor credit assignment in noisy environments. The rubric-based approach confines reasoning to bounded, interpretable condition-action rules. Each evolution round involves backtesting the prior rubric, identifying worst-case scenarios via attribution, proposing atomic rule mutations, and validating via walk-forward gates. This process maps P&L feedback directly to symbolic rule updates, enabling both dynamic adaptation and full auditability. The tri-agent system—rubric evolution, attribution diagnosis, and walk-forward validation—creates a closed-loop governance mechanism that mitigates variance-induced drift while preserving interpretability. In GSE contexts, this translates to a policy engine capable of self-improvement without losing traceability of decisions.
